title: observability-token-kv-metrics-tracing-dashboard-alert-tuning-enhancements
author: Lena Zhou
description: Add finer-grained token-level KV and cost/latency metrics, improve tracing spans for request->response token flow, ship Grafana dashboards and tuned alerting rules to reduce noisy SRE alerts. Motivation: recent incidents and customer feedback showed gaps in per-token KV cache visibility and noisy alerts during planned capacity bursts. This PR introduces new Prometheus recording rules for token-level cost and latency breakdowns, a set of Grafana dashboard panels for model/version/route slicing, updated alert thresholds with smart suppression windows and runbook links, and small telemetry schema compatibility shims. Implementation notes: metrics are exported under redwood_inference_token_* and redwood_inference_kv_* with new labels (model, model_version, route, deployment_tier); recording rules aggregate token cost by route and model_version to make dashboards and alerts cheaper to query; tracing changes add a token_index tag and wire span propagation for helper workers; dashboards include panels for token cost per 1k tokens, KV hit/miss rate per model, per-shard GPU utilization for active serving pools, and top-10 latency contributors. Alert tuning: lower-priority SLO alerts now use a 15m window with 5m evaluation to reduce false positives during autoscaling, KV-miss spike alerts are rate-limited and runbook links point to the playbook. Backwards compatibility: metric renames are additive and we provide compatibility aliases for legacy queries. Tests: unit tests for metrics name generation, small integration test that verifies recording rules produce expected series on synthetic traffic, manual verification of dashboards in staging. Rollout plan: staged rollout to staging -> canary -> prod; dashboards made available in grafana/redwood/observability and alerts applied in two waves. Related Linear: ENG-4521, ENG-4620.
